cards.text: Midian is beaten, and the Israelites come to Gideon with a BIG offer: “Rule over us—you and your son and grandson—for you have saved us from the hand of Midian.” Three generations, a whole family business! Nobody ever offered ME a throne, friend; the best I ever got was a twenty-five cent price sticker.

cards.question: The Israelites want Gideon, his son and his grandson to rule over them. What's Gideon's answer?

answers.text: The LORD will rule over you
My son will rule in my place
I will rule until Midian is gone

cards.text: So Gideon says no to the crown. Then he adds a request: each man gives him an earring from his plunder.

cards.question: Gideon asks for earrings from the plunder. The enemies had ___ earrings because they were Ishmaelites.
When Gideon asks each man for an earring, the Israelites grumble and hold on to their plunder.

cards.text: Earring after earring lands on a spread-out garment: 1,700 shekels of gold, plus crescent ornaments, pendants, the purple garments of Midian's kings and the chains off the camels' necks. Even the CAMELS had to hand over their jewelry!

cards.question: Gideon now has a mountain of gold and royal goods. What does he make from it all?
Gideon places his ephod in Ophrah, his hometown. What does all Israel soon start doing there?
Once Israel worships Gideon's ephod, it became a snare to Gideon and his ___.

cards.text: Meanwhile, Midian is down, and it STAYS down. It never raises its head again.

cards.question: With Midian subdued, the land had rest for ___ years in the days of Gideon.

cards.text: Then Jerubbaal son of Joash, that's Gideon, goes home and settles down. Quiet retirement, right? Ohhh, friend. Not exactly.

cards.question: Back home, Gideon had ___ sons of his own, since he had many wives.

cards.text: SEVENTY sons. I raised six little cookie cutters and thought my counter was CROWDED! And there's one more son, born to Gideon's concubine.

cards.question: Gideon's concubine, the mother of his one more son, lived with him in Ophrah.

cards.text: She lives in Shechem, and Gideon names the boy Abimelech. Later, Gideon dies at a ripe old age and is buried in the tomb of his father Joash in Ophrah.

cards.question: As soon as Gideon is dead, what do the Israelites do?

answers.text: Set up Baal-berith as their god
Ask Gideon's sons to lead them

cards.question: After Gideon dies, the Israelites remember the LORD their God who delivered them from all their enemies on every side.
Gideon did a lot of good for Israel. How do the Israelites treat the house of Jerubbaal after he's gone?

answers.text: They give it land in Ophrah
They make it rich with gold

cards.text: Seventy sons, one more in Shechem and a nation that forgot. Hang onto your apron, friend, because this story is FAR from finished.

findings.problem: The joke calls back to a twenty-five cent price sticker. That detail isn't set up earlier in this lesson, and onboarding only establishes that he spent years in a junk drawer.

rule.text: A callback only works if its setup came earlier in this lesson or conversation.

findings.problem: The card opens with "So Gideon says no to the crown," which tells Judges 8:23, but the card cites only Judges 8:24. It should cite Judges 8:23-24.

rule.text: Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

findings.problem: The card says Gideon "says no to the crown." The text only says he refuses to rule over them and never mentions a crown or a king.

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them.

findings.problem: The question calls the plunder "a mountain of gold." This exaggerates the text in a setup line, not in one of Papa Dorin's own jokes.

rule.text: Don't stretch the text. Exaggerate only in his own jokes.

findings.problem: The blank asks the baker to finish the wording of the line "a snare to Gideon and his ___." Nothing earlier sets up "snare" or who it trapped, so this tests unseen wording rather than meaning the baker can reason out.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: The story card has four sentences: "Then Jerubbaal... settles down." "Quiet retirement, right?" "Ohhh, friend." "Not exactly."

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: "Not exactly" undercuts the text right after it says Gideon returned home and settled down (Judges 8:29). It suggests his settling down wasn't what the text says.

rule.text: Papa Dorin can retell in his own words and fill in what the text clearly implies. Scene-setting details are fine. He never says anything the text shows is wrong.

findings.problem: The story card has three sentences: "SEVENTY sons." "I raised six little cookie cutters..." "And there's one more son..."

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: Nothing earlier gives the baker any way to reason out where the concubine lived, so the true or false is a coin flip. The wording "his one more son" is also awkward.

rule.text: Before each choice card, Papa Dorin's story card gives enough context that the baker can reason their way to the answer.

findings.problem: The right answer "Set up Baal-berith as their god" stands out. It carries a biblical proper name, while the wrong answers are plain descriptions.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike. None should sound more like the Bible, or more modern, than the others.

findings.problem: The last card opens with a recap of the passage: "Seventy sons, one more in Shechem and a nation that forgot." It also cites only Judges 8:35 while summing up Judges 8:30-35.
Putting "Seventy sons" and "one more in Shechem" in front of "this story is FAR from finished" points the baker toward what happens next between Abimelech and his brothers.

rule.text: It gives nothing away about what happens next.

findings.problem: Too many choice cards can only be answered by luck. Card 4 (gold earrings), card 7 (ephod), card 9 (household), card 11 (forty years), card 13 (seventy sons) and card 15 (where the concubine lived) give the baker nothing to reason from. That is about half of the stop's 12 choice cards, not a few.

rule.text: A few discovery questions are fine. Some moments can't be reasoned out, like where Jonah's ship is headed. A few of those are okay, as long as most choice cards are informed guesses.
